title: 3-D Shapes
dadNotes: A face is a flat or curved surface, an edge is where 2 faces meet, a vertex is a corner.
Real boxes help: stick a sticky note on each face so nothing is counted twice.
Schools usually say a cylinder has 3 faces (2 flat, 1 curved) and 2 edges.

lines: Space supply crates are often cubes.
Look at the flat sides of this one.
steps.question: What shape is each flat side?
reveal: Squares! The yellow one has 4 equal sides.
A flat side is called a face.

steps.text: Have you counted faces, edges and vertices at school?

steps.prompt: How many faces does a cube have?
reveal: Top, bottom and 4 around the sides.

say: A face is a flat side.
Tap each face. Spin it to find more.
then: Every face of a cube is a square.
hint: Look underneath and at the back.

say: An edge is where 2 faces meet.
hint: Tap right on the dark lines.
Spin it to find the back ones.
Spin it to find the corners at the back.
Tap each flat side. It turns yellow.
Spin it to find the square underneath.

then: {vertices} vertices. 1 is right at the top.
hint: Tap each corner. Spin it to see them all.
Look at the very top too.

say: How many edges does it have?
Tap to count, then type it.
then: 8 edges: 4 round the base, 4 up to the point.
hint: Tap each edge. A blue number counts it.
Spin it to see both triangle ends.

then: {edges} edges: 3 on each triangle and 3 joining them.
hint: Tap each edge where 2 faces meet.
Spin it to find the edges at the back.

say: A cylinder has flat and curved faces.
hint: The curved face goes all the way round.
Spin it to find the circle underneath.

intro: Your turn. Spin, tap and count.
{engineer} counted the edges of a cube.
fix: The 4 edges going up the sides were missed.

steps.title: Box detective
steps: Stick a note on each face.
How many notes did you use?
Run a finger along each edge and count.
steps.why: Sticky notes help you count each face once and only once.

debrief: What is the difference between a face and an edge?
